inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision; Reasoner ALIGN may then rebuild the evidence synthesis when useful. Completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.
Videos v1, v2 are normalized inputs from one source asset; retain each input identity. Compare timestamps only when another protocol rule explicitly declares a shared clock.
v1 is the beginning and v2 is the ending of one story; infer the missing event from visible before/after state changes rather than treating them as synchronized views.

findings.statement: Video 1 begins with an engine-failure warning, a small glowing-eyed robot, a dark-haired astronaut exiting a spacecraft, and astronauts reacting with alarm amid smoke.
Video 1 shows astronauts moving across rocky terrain with a glowing structure, including a lead astronaut who stops and turns while others continue.
Video 2 shows astronauts walking across dark terrain toward a lit structure and stopping with concerned expressions.
Video 2 includes a green-suited figure and a black-suited astronaut walking through a corridor with a small robot and turning to face each other.
Video 2 shows a grey-haired man activating a console while another watches, followed by close-up console controls.
Both videos show astronaut traversal on dark rocky terrain toward illuminated structures, supporting continuity between the beginning and ending.

open_questions.question: Whether the green-suited figure in the ending is visually linked to the dark-haired astronaut/protagonist from the beginning as a duplicate, clone, or identity-related character remains unresolved.
Whether the ending console activation is tied to revealing the robot or mech pilot identity or to another machine function remains unresolved.
